label: refuter-cyclic-torsion-conjugacy
tail:
No fatal findings.

1. **`thm-free-groups-are-torsion-free` — Fact `[L2]`, proof steps 4.1 and 5.1, and proof contract — nonfatal.**

   Step 4.1 transports the result to an arbitrary free group using `[L3]`, but `[L3]` applies only to two free groups. The displayed `[L2]` merely says:

   > “The reduced words … form a group when the product … is concatenation followed by free reduction.”

   The cited theorem’s actual Statement additionally says:

   > “The map sending \(x\in X\) to the one-letter word \(x\) has the universal property of the free group on \(X\).”

   That omitted clause is what establishes that the reduced-word model satisfies `[L3]`’s premise. The proof contract quotes the full source but assigns `[L2]` only to steps 1.1 and 3.1; step 4.1’s input map likewise omits it.

   Separately, step 5.1 concludes “infinite order” without an explicit Fact reproducing `def-order-in-a-group`, whose Definition says that \(g\) has infinite order exactly when no positive natural power equals the identity.

   The theorem remains true and the existing dependencies supply both missing clauses, so these are licensing/citation gaps closable well within 30 seconds, not fatal defects. The identity, \(n=0\), \(n=1\), empty-generator, and cyclic-seam cases are otherwise correct.

2. **`thm-conjugacy-of-cyclically-reduced-words` — Fact `[L1]` and proof step 5.1 — nonfatal.**

   Step 5.1 transports the reduced-word criterion to every free group using `[L2]`. But `[L2]` only says free groups on the same set are isomorphic, while the displayed `[L1]` only says the reduced words form a group. Neither displayed Fact establishes that the reduced-word group is itself free.

   Again, the actual Statement of `thm-reduced-words-form-the-free-group` supplies exactly the missing universal-property clause quoted above. The proof contract quotes that full target for `[L1]`, but the item’s displayed `[L1]` omits it. This is a nonfatal fact-fidelity/licensing gap; the forward and reverse conjugacy arguments themselves are sound.

3. **`thm-conjugacy-of-cyclically-reduced-words` — proof contract boundary dispositions — nonfatal.**

   In `research/freegroups-1-proof-contracts.json`, the `one` disposition says a one-letter word has only itself as a cyclic shift, although no proof step explicitly anchors that boundary. More concretely, `nonempty-choice` says:

   > “One conjugator is instantiated and its natural length minimized.”

   The proof never minimizes a conjugator: step 1.2 merely takes the given conjugator as its reduced-word representative, and steps 1.3–4.1 induct on an arbitrary reduced conjugator. The proof does not need minimization, so this is an inaccurate contract record rather than a mathematical gap. The batch and merged contract files are byte-identical here.

## 2. Items read and accept

- `def-cyclically-reduced-word` — checked the empty word, one-letter words, empty alphabet, and both formulations using cyclic rotations.
- `lem-cyclic-reduction-normal-form` — checked that the empty input is explicitly outside the Statement; a nonempty reduced word cannot peel to an empty core because step 1.3 leaves a nonempty reduced \(u\); an already cyclically reduced word uses \(t=\varepsilon\); and the noncyclic case explicitly constructs the conjugator \(t=at'\).

## 3. Anything I could not verify

None. Every direct dependency was accessible and read in full. No assigned item relies on an `ai-generated` Statement, computability machinery, or a redefinition of the published universal-property notion of free group.
